title: Ambient nitrogen fixation at industrial rate, efficiency, and lifetime

concept.text: The innovation would make ammonia continuously from atmospheric dinitrogen and a hydrogen source at ambient or near-ambient pressure, while combining industrial production rates, competitive whole-process energy use, and multi-year equipment life. Ammonia converts nitrogen into a form usable for fertilizer and chemical manufacturing. The target is an integrated production capability: a reactor that works quickly and selectively, remains stable, and produces recoverable ammonia without excessive energy or maintenance costs.

Lithium-mediated electrochemistry provides a demonstrated route toward this goal. An electrically driven lithium-containing interface enables nitrogen conversion, with a proton source supplying the hydrogen needed to form ammonia. Its operation depends on a solid-electrolyte interphase, a surface layer whose stability and transport properties influence how lithium ions, nitrogen, and a proton shuttle reach the reaction region. Laboratory continuous-flow ammonia production at ambient pressure has been demonstrated, but that achievement alone does not establish the proposed industrial combination.

Scope synthesis: success would require comparison with ammonia made using electrolytic hydrogen and a Haber–Bosch synthesis loop under equivalent accounting boundaries. Nitrogen and water could be the ultimate inputs, or hydrogen could be supplied separately with its production energy included. Lithium-mediated chemistry is an evidenced candidate route rather than a required definition of the innovation; another process could meet the same capability.

significance.text: Ammonia's established roles in fertilizer and the chemical industry make a major improvement in its manufacture consequential. If near-ambient nitrogen fixation achieved competitive energy use, sustained throughput, and durable operation together, it could support a substantially different production architecture built around modular electrochemical reactors. The transformative feature would be making useful quantities of ammonia under those combined conditions, beyond simply demonstrating that nitrogen can be reduced at low pressure.

Conditional impact synthesis: such reactors could expand the options for producing fertilizer closer to demand and for using ammonia as an energy carrier. Those outcomes would still depend on capital cost, nitrogen preparation, hydrogen supply where applicable, product recovery, storage, transport, and operating conditions. The electrolyzer stack would influence plant size, but the proposed breakthrough does not establish that it alone would determine the minimum economic scale. Economically attractive distributed production and ammonia energy storage therefore remain downstream possibilities.

Impact limits synthesis: comparison with Haber–Bosch is useful because both capabilities concern large-scale conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia. It does not imply that a successful electrochemical reactor would automatically replace the fertilizer system or solve agricultural emissions. Farm deployment, nutrient management, and nitrous-oxide emissions would require separate assessment. Ammonia contains no carbon, but that molecular property does not establish low lifecycle emissions: electricity, feedstocks, construction, and operation remain relevant. Nor would this nitrogen-fixation breakthrough establish a single platform for olefins, aromatics, polymers, and liquid fuels.

The research attributes substantial global importance to ammonia using IEA figures: approximately 2% of final energy use, or 8.6 EJ; about 450 million tonnes of direct CO2 emissions; average production energy near 41 GJ per tonne versus roughly 28 GJ per tonne for a natural-gas best-available route; and approximately 70% of ammonia going to fertilizer. It also attributes historical large-scale electrolysis-based production to the IEA and an approximately threefold cost premium over conventional production to its 2025 fertilisers report. Neither IEA source has retained text in the supplied evidence, so these figures and historical and cost attributions remain unverified here. They provide provisional context rather than established quantitative premises for this record.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is simultaneous performance: continuous near-ambient ammonia production at industrial current density and electrode area, with whole-process energy per tonne competitive with electrolytic-hydrogen Haber–Bosch and a credible multi-year service life. High selectivity, a short period at high current, or long operation in a small cell addresses only part of that target. The supplied laboratory evidence establishes a baseline but does not determine whether later work elsewhere has achieved the complete capability.

Documented barriers in the lithium-mediated route include solvent degradation and the stability of the electrode interface. The reviewed abstract identifies polymerization and volatility of tetrahydrofuran as obstacles to long-term production. The supplementary text describes the need to balance transport of lithium ions, nitrogen, and ethanol through an evolving solid-electrolyte interphase. A protective layer must stabilize operation while allowing the required reactants and charge carriers to move through it. Anodic solvent stability also matters when integrating the reduction reaction with the oxidation side of the cell.

Engineering synthesis: nitrogen's strong triple bond remains a central activation challenge, while full-cell voltage and losses become decisive when the cathode is paired with a practical oxidation reaction involving water or hydrogen. However, the supplied excerpts do not establish the relative importance of these barriers across every candidate process. Scale-up must additionally maintain reactant transport, current distribution, solvent and interface stability, and ammonia recovery across larger electrodes and multiple cells. A high Faradaic efficiency—the fraction of electrical charge that forms ammonia—does not by itself imply low energy use per tonne, because voltage, feed preparation, recovery, and auxiliary loads also contribute.

current_state.text: Li, Zhou, Fu, and colleagues reported a dated laboratory demonstration in Nature 629, 92–97, published online on 19 March 2024. Their flow electrolyzer operated continuously for 300 hours with a 25 cm² electrode at 1 bar and room temperature. The abstract reports current-to-ammonia efficiency of 64 ± 1% and approximately 98% of the produced ammonia in the gas phase. These results demonstrate sustained ambient-pressure synthesis at laboratory scale; the gas-phase share describes where the ammonia was collected, not a product purity of 98%.

The validated review reports additional primary evidence from the retained supplementary-information text. Table S4 gives 4678.4 mg of total ammonia after 300 hours, a gas-phase share of 98.2%, and Faradaic efficiency of 64.4%. Table S8 reports energy efficiency of 17.0% for that demonstration. A Nature Chemical Engineering research highlight published on 10 June 2024 independently summarizes production of more than 4.6 g over 300 hours and 17% energy efficiency. These are reported experimental efficiencies; the supplied evidence does not establish an equivalent whole-process energy comparison with Haber–Bosch.

The evidence available through the supplied review is broader than abstract-only access but narrower than full inspection of the research. The Nature main-article material is a subscription preview containing the abstract. Its supplementary-information text was fully retained and supports the numerical tables and interface discussion, but its figure graphics were not inspected. The Nature Chemical Engineering highlight is also a subscription preview and is secondary reporting. These access boundaries support the stated laboratory results without implying full main-paper or graphical verification.

The research also cites Zhang and colleagues in Science 391, 724–729, dated 12 February 2026, and attributes to that paper 98% Faradaic efficiency and 21% energy efficiency at 100 mA cm⁻², together with 80% Faradaic efficiency maintained for 40 hours before decline. No source text for this citation was retained in the supplied evidence, so its bibliographic details, operating conditions, and numerical claims cannot be verified here. The missing text is an evidence limitation, not evidence that the reported result is false.

Evidence-bounded synthesis: the verified 2024 experiment does not meet the proposed joint industrial throughput, energy, and lifetime target. It produced grams of ammonia over hundreds of hours on tens of square centimeters of electrode area. The supplied record contains no retained contemporary search results that would establish the strongest demonstration as of 1 November 2026 or justify a field-wide conclusion that no later result closes the gap. The innovation remains a coherent target, while its present-day achievement status cannot be settled from this evidence alone.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration, not an established standard: an integrated continuous-flow system would operate at ambient or explicitly specified modest pressure, use nitrogen and water or hydrogen as feeds, and combine at least one square meter of total active electrode area with production on the order of tonnes of ammonia per day for thousands of hours. Electrode area would be sized consistently with the claimed current density and production rate; the one-square-meter floor does not itself imply tonne-per-day output. Area, throughput, pressure, temperature, current density, availability, and degradation would all be reported for the same campaign.
completion_criteria.label: Continuous tonne-per-day ammonia production over thousands of hours

completion_criteria.text: Proposed accounting requirement: closed mass and energy balances would report ammonia production and recovery, recovered-product purity, Faradaic efficiency, whole-process energy per tonne, and carbon intensity. Boundaries would include nitrogen preparation, hydrogen production and delivery where used, product recovery, solvent and electrolyte replenishment, and auxiliary loads. Whole-process energy use would be at or below a same-site electrolytic-hydrogen Haber–Bosch benchmark evaluated with equivalent inputs, product specifications, and accounting boundaries. Reported cell energy efficiency alone would not establish this comparison.
completion_criteria.label: Closed balances show whole-process energy matching or beating electrolytic-hydrogen Haber–Bosch

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and reproducibility requirement: independent reproduction or independently witnessed operation would confirm sustained ammonia output, feed origin, material consumption, and performance degradation. Separate records for selectivity, rate, and lifetime would not satisfy the combined target. Thousands of hours would establish an important durability milestone, with additional long-duration operating evidence and maintenance and replacement data needed to support the multi-year service-life objective.
completion_criteria.label: Independent verification confirms sustained ammonia production and durability together

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: demonstrations would specify feed purity, operating range, product concentration, maintenance intervals, safety provisions, and tolerance to realistic changes in load and feed conditions. Results across multiple cells, campaigns, and operating points would establish demonstrated breadth rather than literal universality. The 2024 laboratory result provides a useful reference point, including its reported 17% energy efficiency, but neither it nor the proposed thresholds establishes that this industrial demonstration is feasible today.
completion_criteria.label: Practical operating limits and demonstrated breadth are explicitly reported

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CHE-03, “Fossil-parity olefins and liquid fuels from carbon dioxide,” shares the ambition of replacing fossil-dependent chemical production with competitive alternative processes. CHE-01 concerns conversion of nitrogen to ammonia; CHE-03 concerns carbon-containing products and requires separate reaction pathways and evidence. CHE-02, “High-yield direct oxidation of methane to methanol with dioxygen,” likewise shares challenges in selective molecular activation and reactor integration, but its feedstocks, chemistry, and product are distinct. Neither entry is subsumed by successful nitrogen fixation.

Roster-based synthesis: CHE-04, “Plant-scale molecular separations that can retire the hardest distillations,” could overlap through ammonia recovery and purification, which influence whole-process energy and economics. CHE-05, “First-time-right scale-up of multiphase reactors,” overlaps through coupled transport, interfaces, and the transition from small electrodes to industrial systems. These are potentially enabling capabilities; success in separation or reactor prediction would not by itself demonstrate efficient, durable nitrogen fixation.

Roster-based synthesis: CHE-06, “Direct solar manufacture of fuels and chemicals,” overlaps if sunlight directly powers a nitrogen-to-ammonia pathway. CHE-01 does not require direct solar conversion and could use electricity from other sources. CHE-08, “Land-free staple calories from carbon dioxide and renewable energy,” has a possible systems connection through nitrogen nutrients, but ammonia production does not establish conversion of carbon dioxide into food.

Roster-based synthesis: CHE-07, “Closed-loop monomers from real mixed plastic waste,” CHE-09, “Direct air capture near the thermodynamic limit, at climate scale,” and CHE-10, “On-demand manufacturing of arbitrary small molecules,” share broader concerns about energy, selectivity, separation, scale, or manufacturing flexibility. Their defining targets remain distinct: waste-to-monomer recovery, dilute atmospheric CO2 capture, and broad molecular synthesis. CHE-01 is a specific nitrogen-to-ammonia production capability. These comparisons use the supplied titles; detailed records for the other concepts were not provided.

change_log.change: Preserved CHE-01's identity and industrial nitrogen-fixation target while distinguishing demonstrated laboratory chemistry from the proposed integrated capability.
change_log.reason: The evidence supports ambient-pressure synthesis without establishing industrial energy competitiveness, throughput, and multi-year life together.

change_log.change: Replaced field-wide claims about the strongest demonstrations and the absence of a successful 2026 result with a bounded account of the supplied evidence.

change_log.reason: The validated review identifies fully retained supplementary text in addition to the partial main-article preview.

change_log.change: Clarified that the approximately 98% gas-phase share is not ammonia product purity.
change_log.reason: Product distribution and recovered-product composition are different measurements.

change_log.reason: No source text was retained, but missing evidence does not establish that the reported findings are false.

change_log.reason: Neither IEA source has retained text, and the quotation's source attribution was inconsistent.

change_log.change: Qualified distributed production, energy-carrier applications, and minimum economic scale as conditional consequences.
change_log.reason: Capital cost, feed preparation, recovery, storage, and logistics remain material determinants beyond electrolyzer performance.

change_log.change: Integrated documented solvent and interphase transport barriers while qualifying the proposed hierarchy of nitrogen-activation and full-cell energy barriers.
change_log.reason: The reviewed excerpts support specific lithium-mediated challenges but do not rank limitations across all candidate processes.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed demonstration to require equivalent whole-process accounting, simultaneous performance, product purity, reproducibility, and additional evidence for multi-year life.
change_log.reason: Cell efficiency and thousands of operating hours alone do not establish plant-level competitiveness or multi-year service.

change_log.change: Clarified that electrode area must be consistent with current density and tonne-per-day output, and added title-based distinctions across the supplied roster.
change_log.reason: An area floor is not a throughput guarantee, and related enabling capabilities should remain separate concepts.

unresolved_issues: Whether any work after the verified 2024 demonstration has achieved the joint target remains unresolved because the supplied record contains no retained contemporary search evidence.
The cited 2026 Science paper's bibliographic details, efficiencies, current density, durability, and operating conditions require source-text verification.
The IEA energy, emissions, fertilizer-share, historical deployment, and cost attributions remain unverified; the original quotation's correct attribution is also unresolved.
The reported laboratory energy-efficiency calculation has not been established as comparable to a complete electrolytic-hydrogen Haber–Bosch process under equivalent boundaries.
The relative importance of nitrogen activation, cathode and anode losses, solvent stability, and interphase transport across candidate processes remains unsettled by the supplied excerpts.

The proposed pressure range, industrial current-density target, plant sizing, and acceptable degradation and maintenance limits need application-specific definition; the numerical demonstration thresholds are proposals rather than established standards.
Detailed technical overlap with other roster entries, especially CHE-03, cannot be confirmed from titles alone.
